{"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-08: Finance Events — Lifecycle and Auto-Creation Triggers\n\nWalks the full finance event state machine and idempotent creation:\n  1. Create fee type catalogue entries\n  2. Create a finance event directly (charge) → draft\n  3. Confirm the event → 'confirmed'\n  4. Settle the event → 'settled'\n  5. Create a second event and cancel it → 'cancelled' (cannot be settled)\n  6. Use create_from_source() — idempotent: second call returns same record\n  7. Mark exported → handoff_state = 'exported'\n  8. Mark reconciled → handoff_state = 'reconciled'\n\nKey invariants verified:\n- State transitions: draft → confirmed → settled\n- Cancelled events cannot be settled (raises ValidationError or ignored)\n- create_from_source() is idempotent (same external_ref is skipped)\n- handoff workflow: pending_export → exported → reconciled\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom odoo.exceptions import ValidationError\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\nclass TestTourFinanceLifecycle(TransactionCase):\n    \"\"\"T-08: Finance event lifecycle tour.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Finance Tour Club\", \"code\": \"FTC26\"}\n        )\n        cls.season = cls.env[\"federation.season\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Finance Tour Season\",\n                \"code\": \"FTS26\",\n                \"date_start\": \"2026-01-01\",\n                \"date_end\": \"2026-12-31\",\n            }\n        )\n\n        # Fee types covering all categories\n        cls.fee_registration = cls.env[\"federation.fee.type\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Registration Fee\",\n                \"code\": \"TOUREG\",\n                \"category\": \"registration\",\n                \"default_amount\": 150.00,\n            }\n        )\n        cls.fee_fine = cls.env[\"federation.fee.type\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Fine\",\n                \"code\": \"TOUFIN\",\n                \"category\": \"fine\",\n                \"default_amount\": 100.00,\n            }\n        )\n\n    def test_finance_event_full_lifecycle(self):\n        \"\"\"Finance events: draft → confirmed → settled; cancel; idempotent create; handoff.\"\"\"\n\n        # STEP 1: Create a charge event manually\n        event = self.env[\"federation.finance.event\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Registration 2026\",\n                \"fee_type_id\": self.fee_registration.id,\n                \"event_type\": \"charge\",\n                \"amount\": 150.00,\n                \"source_model\": \"federation.club\",\n                \"source_res_id\": self.club.id,\n                \"club_id\": self.club.id,\n                \"season_id\": self.season.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(event.state, \"draft\")\n        self.assertEqual(event.handoff_state, \"pending_export\")\n\n        # STEP 2: Confirm → immutable amounts\n        event.action_confirm()\n        self.assertEqual(event.state, \"confirmed\")\n\n        # STEP 3: Settle\n        event.action_settle()\n        self.assertEqual(event.state, \"settled\")\n\n        # STEP 4: Create a second event and cancel it\n        event2 = self.env[\"federation.finance.event\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Fine — Contested\",\n                \"fee_type_id\": self.fee_fine.id,\n                \"event_type\": \"charge\",\n                \"amount\": 100.00,\n                \"source_model\": \"federation.club\",\n                \"source_res_id\": self.club.id,\n                \"club_id\": self.club.id,\n            }\n        )\n        event2.action_cancel()\n        self.assertEqual(event2.state, \"cancelled\")\n\n        # Cancelled events cannot be settled\n        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):\n            event2.action_settle()\n\n        # STEP 5: create_from_source() — idempotent\n        src_event = self.env[\"federation.finance.event\"].create_from_source(\n            source_record=self.club,\n            fee_type=self.fee_registration,\n        )\n        self.assertTrue(src_event.id)\n        self.assertEqual(src_event.source_model, \"federation.club\")\n        self.assertEqual(src_event.source_res_id, self.club.id)\n\n        # {"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any record type via model/res_id.\n5. **Outcome evidence** — implemented requests now create outcome-log rows so\n   governance review can extend beyond the approval moment.\n", "content_length": 3754, {"content": "Sports Federation Import Tools\n==============================\n\nWizard-driven CSV import for clubs, seasons, teams, players, and tournament\nparticipants. The module is intended for federation onboarding and annual\nrollover work where administrators need rehearsable imports instead of raw ORM\nloads.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nThe import wizards provide a safer operator workflow than direct list imports:\n\n- dry-run rehearsal before any records are created\n- approval checkpoints before live imports execute\n- visible column mapping guidance in the wizard form\n- code-first reference lookup where the target models expose stable codes\n- categorized row-level failures instead of opaque batch errors\n- duplicate-safe behavior that reports and skips existing records\n- reusable template records that define the import contract per wizard\n- governance-job verification summaries with before/after target counts\n- managed partner contracts with token-authenticated subscriptions\n- staged inbound deliveries that reuse the same governed preview and approval\n  pipeline\n\nThe menu entry is available at ``Federation > Import Tools``.\nThe transient import models now live under the standard ``wizards/`` package to\nmatch the rest of the repository.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs, seasons, teams.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournament participants.\n\nShared Wizard Behaviour\n-----------------------\n\nAll import wizards inherit ``federation.import.wizard.mixin``.\n\nShared capabilities:\n\n- UTF-8 and UTF-8 BOM CSV decoding.\n- Comma or semicolon delimiter support.\n- Reusable ``federation.import.template`` selection.\n- Checksum-bound ``federation.import.job`` approval workflow for live imports.\n- Shared fields: ``dry_run``, ``mapping_guide``, ``result_message``,\n  ``line_count``, ``success_count``, and ``error_count``.\n- Shared ``_execute_row_create(...)`` handling so live imports reuse one\n  row-create failure path instead of ad hoc wizard-level try/except blocks.\n- Standardized error categories such as ``missing_reference``,\n  ``duplicate_entry``, ``format_error``, and ``missing_required_field``.\n- Explicit compatibility handling for legacy CSV aliases tracked in\n  ``INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md``.\n\nManaged Partner Integrations\n----------------------------\n\nThe module also provides a managed integration layer for machine-driven import\nand export contracts.\n\nCore models:\n\n- ``federation.integration.contract`` defines the contract code, version,\n  direction, transport, route hint, availability requirements, and optional\n  linked import allowed to use.\n- ``federation.integration.delivery`` stages inbound partner payloads and links\n  them to the downstream governance job.\n\nCurrent model layout:\n\n- entry point.\n- ``models/integration_partner_token_mixin.py`` keeps token generation,\n  hashing, verification, migration, and hashed persistence hooks.\n- duplicate reuse, and attachment creation.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_workflow_mixin.py`` keeps wizard handoff and\n  delivery state transitions.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_retention_mixin.py`` keeps retention cleanup.\n\nCurrent wizard layout:\n\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_mixin.py`` remains the stable shared surface used by\n  all import wizards.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_csv_mixin.py`` keeps CSV parsing, column validation,\n  row helpers, and shared error taxonomy.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_governance_mixin.py`` keeps approval checks,\n  governance-job persistence, and result finalization.\n\nCurrent controller layout:\n\n- ``controllers/integration_api.py`` keeps the stable public route surface and\n  route-level orchestration.\n- ``controllers/integration_api_auth_mixin.py`` keeps header parsing, partner\n  authentication, caller identity, and rate-limit subject helpers.\n- Migration risk:\n  none, because this is a file-layout change only.\n- Rules completed: delivery staging, idempotency, workflow handoff, and\n  retention cleanup now live in dedicated helper mixins while\n  ``federation.integration.delivery`` keeps the ORM contract stable. Test\n  impact: inbound delivery staging, idempotency, and retention coverage stays\n  green. {"content": "# Match-Day Operations\n\nThis addon executes the current immutable schedule publication. It never edits\napproved publication evidence.\n\n## Operator workflow\n\n- **Match-Day Control** shows readiness and the exact live publication.\n- **Open Match Day** validates the publication digest and creates an immutable\n  execution session.\n- Court status and incidents are changed through command-backed wizards.\n- Operational schedule changes support move, delay, postpone and cancel.\n- Every deviation requires a reason and records the session, publication, actor,\n  old slot and new slot.\n- The immutable `published_slot_id` is preserved. Live reality is represented by\n  `operational_slot_id` and `operational_status`.\n- Normal close requires all matches finished or cancelled and all incidents\n  resolved. {"content": "# Sports Federation People\n\nPlayer master data and license management for the federation. Tracks every\nregistered player's personal information, club affiliation, and maintains a\ncomplete licensing history across seasons.\n\n## Purpose\n\nProvides the **player** and **player license** models that underpin roster\nmanagement, eligibility checks, discipline tracking, and compliance workflows.\nEvery module that deals with individual athletes depends on People.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- `sports_federation_base`: Clubs, teams, and seasons.\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.player`\n\nMaster record for every registered individual. Names are split into first/last\nfor sorting and flexible display.\n\n- `name`: Char (computed), stored as `last_name, first_name`.\n- `first_name` / `last_name`: Char, legal name parts and both required.\n- `birth_date`: Date of birth.\n- `gender`: Selection with `male`, `female`, or `other`.\n- `nationality_id`: Many2one to the nationality country.\n- `club_id`: Many2one to the current club affiliation.\n- `team_ids`: Many2many teams the player belongs to.\n- `email` / `phone` / `mobile`: Contact channels.\n- `photo`: Binary player photograph.\n- `state`: Selection with `draft`, `active`, `suspended`, or `retired`.\n- `license_ids`: One2many historical license records.\n- `license_count`: Integer stat-button counter.\n- `notes`: Free-form notes.\n\n- **State machine**: draft → active → suspended / retired.\n- **Stat button** navigates to license history.\n\n### `federation.player.license`\n\nSeason-scoped license that proves a player's right to compete. A player may hold\nmultiple licenses across seasons, but only one active license per season applies.\n\n- `name`: Char, auto-generated license number from a sequence.\n- `player_id`: Many2one to the licensed player.\n- `season_id`: Many2one to the covered season.\n- `club_id`: Many2one to the club at time of issue.\n- `issue_date` / `expiry_date`: Date validity window.\n- `state`: Selection with `draft`, `active`, `expired`, or `cancelled`.\n- `category`: Selection for license category such as amateur or professional.\n- `eligibility_notes`: Text eligibility remarks.\n- `notes`: Additional notes.\n\n- License numbers generated via `ir.sequence`.\n- Operator-facing copy should use `cancelled` for invalidated licenses. Older\n   notes may still say `revoked`, but that is compatibility-only wording.\n\n## Data Files\n\n- `data/ir_sequence.xml`: `FED-LIC-` sequence for license numbers.\n- `security/ir.model.access.csv`: CRUD rights for federation groups.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Name computation** — `name` is automatically composed from `last_name` and\n   `first_name` and kept in sync.\n2. **License numbering** — Every new license receives an auto-incremented\n   `FED-LIC-XXXXX` reference via `ir.sequence`.\n3. **Club ↔ Player link** — `club_id` on the player is the *current* affiliation;\n   the license records preserve the historical club at time of issue.\n", "content_length": 2915, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_people/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "28909238ab4d7553ba5922d32d0c903d7ecd966f88949edb478d180d463fa738", "size_bytes": 2927}

{"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n", "content_length": 2994, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "9ff77294460c25ba8798e5b29ecdb05ce6d12c1d7d25ea2bba2462d44b3b9e05", "size_bytes": 2994}

{"content": "# Sports Federation Public Site\n\nPublic website coverage for tournaments, now integrated into the main\nTournaments navigation instead of a separate Competitions surface.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThis module turns published tournaments into a coherent public product for fans,\nclubs, and media. It provides a tournament hub, overview pages, schedule and\nresults pages, standings snapshots, team profile pages, JSON feed access, and\ncalendar export while keeping older competition URLs working.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `website` | Odoo website framework |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Main tournament website hub and navigation |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments, matches, participants |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue information |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Approved result visibility |\n\n## Model extensions\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables public visibility |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Legacy public slug retained for tournament feed and redirect compatibility |\n| `public_description` | Html | Long-form website description |\n| `public_featured` | Boolean | Marks the tournament for featured hub sections |\n| `public_editorial_summary` | Text | Short editorial summary for cards and overview layouts |\n| `public_pinned_announcement` | Text | Announcement banner content for the overview page |\n| `public_hero_image` | Binary | Hero image for the public overview page |\n| `show_public_results` | Boolean | Enables the public results page |\n| `show_public_standings` | Boolean | Enables the public standings page |\n\nKey helper methods expose canonical public URLs, published tournament queries,\nteam/result/standings/schedule datasets, JSON feed payloads, and ICS calendar\nexport content.\n\n### `federation.team`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in `/teams/<slug>` |\n\nTeam helpers provide stable team profile URLs and public tournament links.\nTheir public slug resolver accepts an extra publication domain so controller\nlookups can fail closed before rendering profile, follow, feed, or calendar\nsurfaces.\n\n### `federation.season`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Enables season-wide discovery on the website |\n| `public_slug` | Char | Canonical public slug used in {"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-09: Public Site — Tournament Publication and Editorial Scheduling\n\nWalks the public site publication workflow:\n  1. Create a tournament and publish it (website_published = True)\n  2. Create an editorial item in draft\n  3. Schedule the item → 'scheduled'\n  4. Publish the item → 'published'\n  5. Archive the item → 'archived'\n  6. Reset to draft → 'draft'\n  7. Verify get_live_items() returns only published/in-window items\n\nKey invariants verified:\n- editorial item states: draft → scheduled → published → archived → draft\n- get_live_items() excludes draft and archived items\n- tournament website_published field is settable\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\nclass TestTourPublication(TransactionCase):\n    \"\"\"T-09: Public site publication lifecycle tour.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n\n        cls.season = cls.env[\"federation.season\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Publication Tour Season\",\n                \"code\": \"PUB26\",\n                \"date_start\": \"2026-01-01\",\n                \"date_end\": \"2026-12-31\",\n            }\n        )\n        cls.tournament = cls.env[\"federation.tournament\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Publication Tour Cup\",\n                \"season_id\": cls.season.id,\n                \"date_start\": \"2026-06-01\",\n            }\n        )\n\n    def test_publication_lifecycle(self):\n        \"\"\"Tournament publication + editorial item state machine.\"\"\"\n\n        # {"content": "# Competition Registration\n\nThe Registration Desk manages team entries for a competition edition and division.\n\n## Team selection\n\nWhen creating or editing a competition entry, the team dropdown is limited to:\n\n- active teams;\n- teams eligible for the selected division's category and gender;\n- teams that are not already entered in the same registration window.\n\nThe available-team list is computed per division and the form applies it as a\nselection domain. The model also validates the same rules on create and write,\nso direct ORM or API requests cannot bypass the desk filter. Changing a window\nclears an existing team selection when it is no longer valid.\n\nEligibility uses the tournament module's existing `search_eligible_teams()` and\n`get_team_eligibility_error()` APIs. No historical registration entries are\nrewritten by this filtering; it only affects new selections and invalid direct\nwrites.\n\n## Regression tests\n\nThe regression coverage is in\n`tests/test_registration_team_selection.py`. {"content": "# Sports Federation Reporting\n\nCross-module analytical reports backed by PostgreSQL views plus scheduled report\nsnapshots. Provides read-only report models that aggregate participation,\nofficiating, compliance, finance, and tournament-readiness data into\noperator-facing views.\n\n## Purpose\n\nGives federation administrators a **dashboard-level view** of key metrics without\nwriting SQL or building custom reports. Each report model is a database view\nthat joins and aggregates data from multiple modules into a single, filterable\nlist or pivot view, while report schedules generate recurring weekly or monthly\nCSV snapshots from inside Odoo.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referees, assignments |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Disciplinary data |\n| `sports_federation_compliance` | Compliance data |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Finance events |\n| `sports_federation_import_tools` | Inbound delivery failures for operator checklist reporting |\n\nAudit dashboard surfaces:\n\n- `Reporting > Portal Audit` groups privileged portal create/write/call activity\n\temitted through `federation.portal.privilege`.\n- `Reporting > Token Rotation Audit` groups manager-driven integration partner\n\ttoken rotation events emitted from the import-tools token rotation flow.\n- both dashboards read the shared `federation.audit.event` log so additional\n\taudited workflows can reuse the same reporting contract later.\n\n## Models (all SQL view-backed, `_auto = False`)\n\n### `federation.report.participation`\n\nClub participation summary per season.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Club |\n| `team_count` | Integer | Teams registered |\n| `player_count` | Integer | Players licensed |\n| `tournament_count` | Integer | Tournaments entered |\n\n### `federation.report.officiating`\n\nReferee workload summary.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Referee |\n| `certification_level` | Char | Current level |\n| `assignment_count` | Integer | Total assignments |\n| `completed_assignment_count` | Integer | Completed assignments |\n\n### `federation.report.compliance`\n\nCompliance status overview by entity type.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `target_model` | Char | Entity type |\n| `compliant_count` | Integer | Entities in compliance |\n| `missing_count` | Integer | Missing documents |\n| `pending_count` | Integer | Awaiting review |\n| `expired_count` | Integer | Expired documents |\n| `non_compliant_count` | Integer | Explicitly rejected or non-compliant checks |\n\n### `federation.report.finance`\n\nFinancial event summary by fee type and state.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `fee_type_id` | Many2one | Fee category |\n| `state` | Selection | Event state |\n| `event_count` | Integer | Number of events |\n| `total_amount` | Float | Sum of amounts |\n\n### `federation.report.operational`\n\nTournament-level operational KPI view.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `tournament_id` | Many2one | Scope of the KPI row |\n| `participant_count` / `confirmed_participant_count` | Integer | Enrolment totals |\n| `participant_confirmation_rate` | Float | Confirmed-participant percentage |\n| `match_count` / `completed_match_count` | Integer | Match execution totals |\n| `match_completion_rate` | Float | Completed-match percentage |\n| `pending_finance_event_count` / `pending_finance_amount` | Integer / Float | Open finance follow-up tied to match operations |\n| `open_club_compliance_count` | Integer | Outstanding club compliance checks for participating clubs |\n| `readiness_status` | Selection | `healthy`, `attention`, or `blocked` |\n| `readiness_note` | Text | Operator-readable summary of the active readiness blockers or follow-up work |\n\n### `federation.report.standing.reconciliation`\n\nTournament-level standings coverage check.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `confirmed_participant_count` | Integer | Confirmed tournament participants |\n| `covered_participant_count` | Integer | Distinct participants represented in standings |\n| `missing_participant_count` | Integer | Confirmed participants missing from standings coverage |\n| `orphaned_participant_count` | Integer | Standings entries without a matching confirmed participant |\n| `reconciliation_status` | Selection | `healthy`, `attention`, or `blocked` |\n| `reconciliation_note` | Text | Operator-readable mismatch explanation |\n\n### `federation.report.finance.reconciliation`\n\nFinance follow-up queue by event.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `finance_event_id` | Many2one | Source finance event |\n| `counterparty_display` | Char | Club, player, referee, or partner name |\n| `federation.report.season.checklist`\n\nSeason-by-season readiness checklist for high-volume federation administration.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season being reviewed |\n| `draft_season_registration_count` / `submitted_season_registration_count` | Integer | Season registration work queue |\n| `draft_tournament_registration_count` `attention`, or `blocked` |\n| `checklist_note` | Text | Summary of the main operational blocker |\n\n### `federation.report.season.portfolio`\n\nSeason-level planning portfolio that compares the Year 4 planning baseline with\ncurrent delivery, finance, and compliance position.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `season_state` | Many2one / Selection | Planned season in scope |\n| `target_*` / `actual_*` / `*_delta` | Integer | Planned vs actual clubs, teams, tournaments, and participants |\n| `budget_amount` / `actual_finance_amount` / `budget_variance_amount` | Float | Planned vs actual finance position |\n| `open_compliance_item_count` | Integer | Outstanding compliance load for confirmed clubs |\n| `planning_status` / `planning_note` | Selection / Text | Operator-readable planning health |\n\n### `federation.report.club.performance`\n\nClub-by-club seasonal performance roll-up for tournament activity, results,\nfinance queue load, and compliance attention.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `club_id` | Many2one | Club performance scope |\n| `confirmed_team_count` / `confirmed_tournament_entry_count` | Integer | Seasonal participation footprint |\n| `completed_match_count`, `win_count`, `draw_count`, `loss_count` | Integer | Competitive for the club |\n| `open_compliance_item_count` | Integer | Open club compliance items |\n| `performance_status` / `performance_note` | Selection / Text | Operator-readable club status |\n\n### `federation.report.schedule`\n\nPersistent schedule for recurring application-layer report generation.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `report_type` | Selection | Operational, reconciliation, compliance, board/audit packs, season portfolio, or club performance |\n| `period_type` | Selection | Weekly or monthly cadence |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Optional season scope for season-based reports |\n| `next_run_on` / `last_attempt_on` / `last_run_on` | Datetime | Scheduling metadata and last execution attempt |\n| `last_run_status` | Selection | `never`, `success`, or `failed` |\n| `last_failure_on` / `last_error_message` | Datetime / Text | Persisted failure state for the most recent failed generation |\n| `consecutive_failure_count` | Integer | Number of failed generation attempts in a row |\n| `generated_file` | Binary | Last generated CSV snapshot |\n| `last_row_count` | Integer | Number of exported data rows |\n\nImplementation note:\n\n- Report-type-specific row builders and back-office action metadata now live in `services/report_schedule_builders.py`.\n- Keep new schedule types in that registry so `federation.report.schedule` stays focused on cadence, CSV serialization, retention, and failure capture.\n\nSnapshot/query modernization note:\n\n- `federation.report.snapshot` now computes compliance backlog totals through a\n\tsingle SQL aggregate query (`_compliance_pending_total`) instead of\n\t`read_group` aggregation.\n- Snapshot and schedule cron entrypoints now attach a shared\n\t`federation_correlation_id` context value and emit correlation-aware logs.\n\n### `federation.report.audit.event`\n\nRead-only audit log reporting view for privileged portal activity and\nintegration token rotations.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `event_family` | Selection | `portal_privilege` or `integration_token` |\n| `event_type` / `action_name` | Char | Normalized audit classification and originating method |\n| `actor_user_id` | Many2one | User who triggered the audited action |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` / `target_display_name` | Char / Integer / Char | Record affected by the audited action |\n| `changed_fields` | Text | Comma-separated field names touched by the action when known |\n| `description` | Text | Operator-readable audit summary |\n\n### `federation.report.operator.checklist`\n\nOperator-facing queue roll-up that consolidates the release-critical exception\nsurfaces into a single reporting menu.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `queue_code` / `queue_name` | Selection / Char | Stable identifier and display name for the queue |\n| `owner_display` | Char | Operational owner for the queue |\n| `open_count` / `escalated_count` | Integer | Queue depth and escalated subset |\n| `oldest_age_days` | Integer | Oldest unresolved item age |\n| `status` | Selection | `healthy`, `attention`, or `blocked` |\n| `summary` | Text | Operator-readable explanation of what the queue means |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Read-only views** — Analytical models use `_auto = False` with `init()` creating SQL views.\n2. **Role-oriented reporting surfaces** — Operational KPIs, standings reconciliation, finance reconciliation, and compliance summaries are separated into task-specific menus instead of a single generic export path.\n3. **Cross-module joins** — Operational KPIs combine tournament, standings, finance, and compliance data into one application-layer view.\n4. **Recurring snapshots** — `federation.report.schedule` can generate weekly or monthly CSV snapshots and a daily cron refreshes active schedules.\n5. **Reconciliation-first reporting** — Standings coverage, finance follow-up, failed-notification queues, missing discipline-finance events, and stalled workflow queues expose the specific gaps operators must resolve before relying on downstream outputs.\n6. **Season operations checklist** — The reporting layer now includes a season-level checklist that surfaces review queues, publication gaps, and unresolved workflow exceptions in one place.\n7. **Planning decision support** — Season portfolio and club performance views turn the reporting layer into a planning and delivery-monitoring surface instead of a pure export utility.\n8. **Legacy CSV exports preserved** — The lightweight HTTP CSV endpoints remain available for ad hoc export use.\n9. **Contract-tagged exports** — Authenticated CSV responses now include explicit contract and version headers for downstream consumers.\n10. **Operator checklist** — Notification failures, workflow exceptions, finance follow-up, inbound delivery failures, blocked season readiness, and scheduled report failures now surface in one menu.\n11. **Persistent schedule failure tracking** — Report schedules keep the last failure timestamp, error message, and consecutive failure count so recurring problems survive beyond transient logs.\n12. **Generated-file retention** — Scheduled report artifacts are cleared automatically after the retention window in `DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md`, while the schedule metadata and next run remain intact.\n\n## CSV exports\n\nAuthenticated backend users can export lightweight KPI CSV files from the\nreporting controllers:\n\n- `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>` — standings lines with tie-break notes\n- `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>` — season participation roster\n- `/reporting/export/finance` — finance summary grouped by fee type and state\n- and\n`X-Federation-Contract-Version` headers. The detailed finance-event handoff\nexport uses the `finance_event_v1` contract.\n\nFor recurring in-application reporting, create records under **Federation → Reporting → Report Schedules**.\nEach schedule stores the last generated CSV snapshot directly on the schedule record.\nUse **Federation → Reporting → Operator Checklist** for the release-readiness\nqueue view that links back to the underlying exception surfaces.\n", "content_length": 15828, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_reporting/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "74a20b38e6cb4b156489e215d77a45ee51368d6a217bbd444d4e961119b2545a", "size_bytes": 15868}

{"content": "# Sports Federation Result Control\n\nVersion: 19.0.1.2.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nControlled result lifecycle, audit history, separation of duties, and standings officiality for federation matches.\n\n## Workflow\n\nThe result path supports draft, submission, verification, approval, contest, and correction as implemented by the match result controls. Approved results are protected against uncontrolled mutation.\n\n## Safeguards\n\n- submit, verify, and approve permissions are checked at action time\n- separation-of-duties rules prevent forbidden actor reuse\n- approved-score changes require the correction workflow\n- audit rows retain actor, action, and before/after context\n- standings only consume results that meet the officiality rules\n- contested and corrected paths remain traceable\n\n## Integration\n\nPortal and tournament-operation actions call the same model-owned result methods as backend flows. Standings recomputation follows successful official result transitions.\n\n## Tests\n\nCoverage includes lifecycle transitions, immutability, duty separation, contest/correction recovery, audit records, and end-to-end result pipeline tours.\n\n## Removed document\n\n`ROADMAP_RC.md` is deleted. Approved-result immutability is an implemented invariant and belongs in this README and its regression tests, not a permanent mini-roadmap.\n", "content_length": 1392, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_result_control/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "87bf551e2daeaa57f59eb574314f39b1e0cd3e968b56ed655fa78cd760e1a4c0", "size_bytes": 1392}

{"content": "Sports Federation Rosters\n=========================\n\nSeason and competition-bound team rosters plus match-day squad sheets. Controls\nwhich players are eligible and available for each match, enforces squad-size\nlimits from the applicable rule set, and surfaces operator-readable readiness\nfeedback before rosters, participants, or match sheets move forward.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a formal roster, which is the pool of players a team may select from\nfor a season or competition, and match sheets, which are the specific squad and\nstarting lineup for an individual match. The module links to rule sets for\nsquad-size validation and to the shared eligibility service for license,\nregistration, and suspension checks.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs, teams, and seasons.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Squad-size limits and player eligibility checks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.team.roster``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA pool of eligible players for a team within a season or competition scope.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Generated roster label.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Team.\n- ``season_id`` (Many2one): Season scope.\n- ``season_registration_id`` (Many2one): Linked registration.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Optional competition scope.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Squad-size rules.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``active``, or ``closed``.\n- ``valid_from`` / ``valid_to`` (Date): Validity window.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Rostered players.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Player count.\n- ``club_id`` (Many2one, computed): Derived from the team.\n- ``min_players_required`` / ``max_players_allowed`` (Integer): Limits pulled\n   from the rule set.\n- ``ready_for_activation`` (Boolean, computed): Whether activation checks pass.\n- ``readiness_feedback`` (Text, computed): Aggregated activation blockers.\n- ``match_sheet_count`` (Integer, computed): Linked match sheets using this\n   roster.\n- ``match_day_locked`` (Boolean, computed): Whether live match sheets now lock\n   roster scope changes.\n- ``match_day_lock_feedback`` (Text, computed): Why the roster scope is locked.\n- ``audit_event_ids`` (One2many): Participation audit events for this roster.\n\n``federation.team.roster.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA single player entry on a roster.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Parent roster.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): The player.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``active``, ``inactive``, ``suspended``, or\n   ``removed``.\n- ``date_from`` / ``date_to`` (Date): Availability window.\n- ``jersey_number`` (Char): Squad number.\n- ``is_captain`` / ``is_vice_captain`` (Boolean): Leadership flags.\n- ``license_id`` (Many2one): Explicit season license to validate.\n- ``eligible`` (Boolean, computed): Current eligibility status.\n- ``eligibility_feedback`` (Text, computed): Human-readable failure reasons.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\nKey behaviour:\n\n- Once a submitted, approved, or locked match sheet references a roster line,\n   that referenced line cannot be structurally changed or removed.\n\n``federation.match.sheet``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nThe squad list submitted for a specific match.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Sheet title.\n- ``match_id`` (Many2one): The match.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Which team the sheet belongs to.\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Source roster.\n- ``side`` (Selection): ``home`` or ``away``.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``submitted``, ``approved``, or ``locked``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Player entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Squad size.\n- ``ready_for_submission`` (Boolean, computed): Whether submission checks pass.\n- ``readiness_feedback`` (Text, computed): Aggregated submission blockers.\n- ``substitution_count`` (Integer, computed): Number of recorded substitution\n   entries.\n- ``locked_on`` / ``locked_by_id`` (Datetime / Many2one): Final lock metadata.\n- ``audit_event_ids`` (One2many): Participation audit events for this sheet.\n- ``coach_name`` / ``manager_name`` (Char): Team staff.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> submitted -> approved -> locked``.\n- Submitted sheets may return to draft for operator corrections before\n   approval.\n- Matches created interactively receive draft home and away sheets when the\n   rosters module is installed. Demo data loading runs without this side\n   effect, so explicit fixtures such as the demo pack can define their own\n   sheets without colliding with automatically created records.\n\n``federation.match.sheet.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA player on a match sheet.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``match_sheet_id`` (Many2one): Parent sheet.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): The player.\n- ``roster_line_id`` (Many2one): Source roster line.\n- ``is_starter`` (Boolean): In the starting lineup.\n- ``is_substitute`` (Boolean): Bench selection.\n- ``is_captain`` (Boolean): Match captain.\n- ``jersey_number`` (Char): Shirt number.\n- ``entered_minute`` / ``left_minute`` (Integer): Substitution timeline\n   tracking.\n- ``eligible`` (Boolean, computed): Current eligibility status.\n- ``eligibility_feedback`` (Text, computed): Human-readable failure reasons.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n``federation.participation.audit``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nImmutable operational log for roster and match-sheet activity.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``event_type`` (Selection): Created, updated, submitted, approved, locked,\n   and substitution events.\n- ``team_id`` (Many2one): Team owning the event.\n- ``roster_id`` (Many2one): Related season roster when applicable.\n- ``match_sheet_id`` (Many2one): Related match sheet when applicable.\n- ``match_id`` (Many2one): Related match when applicable.\n- ``player_id`` (Many2one): Player affected by the event.\n- ``description`` (Text): Human-readable audit detail.\n- ``author_id`` / ``event_on`` (Many2one / Datetime): Attribution and\n   timestamp.\n\n``federation.tournament.participant`` Extension\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nThis module extends tournament participants with team-linked roster readiness\nchecks. Tournament registration auto-provisions a team roster for the relevant\nseason and competition scope. Participants can still be confirmed and assigned\nwithout a ready roster before the roster deadline, but once that deadline is\nreached both participant confirmation and scheduled matches require an active\nready roster: one week before the first scheduled match, or one week before the\ntournament start if no match has been scheduled yet.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``ready_for_confirmation`` (Boolean, computed): Whether the linked team\n   currently satisfies the roster deadline rule.\n- ``roster_deadline_date`` (Date, computed): Deadline for having an active\n   ready roster.\n- ``readiness_roster_id`` (Many2one, computed): Preferred team roster used for\n   readiness checks.\n- ``confirmation_feedback`` (Text, computed): Warning or blocking message about\n   the roster deadline.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Roster scoping**: rosters are tied to a season and optionally a\n   competition, preventing cross-competition player sharing.\n- **Eligibility-aware activation**: roster activation is blocked until active\n   lines satisfy date windows, squad-size bounds, and shared eligibility rules.\n- **Readable operator feedback**: roster lines and match-sheet lines expose\n   ``eligibility_feedback``, while rosters and match sheets aggregate blockers\n   into readiness summaries.\n- **Match sheet from roster**: match sheets validate against explicit roster\n   lines so team, date-window, and license mismatches are caught early.\n- **Match-day locking**: submitted and approved sheet activity locks roster\n   scope changes and the referenced roster lines so historical lineups remain\n   defensible.\n- **Undoable closure**: closing a roster is no longer terminal. Federation\n   staff can reopen a closed roster back to active when closure was premature,\n   while active-roster uniqueness and readiness checks still apply.\n- **Substitution governance**: approved sheets can record ``entered_minute``\n   and ``left_minute`` values while still blocking lineup changes after\n   approval.\n- **Participation audit trail**: roster lifecycle changes, lineup changes,\n   submissions, submitted-sheet resets, approvals, locks, and substitutions are\n   captured in ``federation.participation.audit``.\n- **Participant roster readiness**: tournament registration creates or reuses\n   the relevant team roster automatically so roster maintenance stays attached\n   to the participating team instead of requiring a separately named setup step.\n- **Operational roster deadline**: tournament participants can still be\n   confirmed and grouped without a ready roster before the deadline, but once\n   the one-week deadline is reached operators cannot confirm participants or\n   schedule matches until an active ready roster exists.\n- **Guided roster handoff**: confirmed season registrations now open the roster\n   list with the relevant team, season, competition, and rule-set context, and\n   participant forms expose the current roster deadline plus an `Open Team\n   Roster` handoff when readiness work is the next blocker.\n- **Team-linked roster checks**: team roster lookup and tournament deadline\n   assessment are owned by the team model so roster compliance follows the team\n   rather than being treated as a separate participant-only concern.\n- **State locking**: approved match sheets can be locked once match-day\n   operations are complete.\n", "content_length": 9575, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_rosters/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "711f0f8717a7f60ceac6e892e83cdc755ed78745dd4ba852a6b3ae971c2bbe84", "size_bytes": 9575}

{"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-04: Roster Management — Activation, Match Sheet Workflow, Close\n\nWalks the full roster lifecycle for a team:\n  1. Draft roster — activation fails without players\n  2. Add players, activate roster\n  3. Unique-active-roster constraint: second activation attempt raises\n  4. Create a match and a match sheet linked to the active roster\n  5. Create players\n        cls.players = cls.env[\"federation.player\"]\n        for i in range(1, 5):\n            p = cls.env[\"federation.player\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"first_name\": f\"Roster{i}\",\n                    \"last_name\": \"Player\",\n                    \"gender\": \"male\",\n                }\n            )\n            cls.players |= p\n\n    def test_roster_lifecycle_and_match_sheet_workflow(self):\n        \"\"\"Roster draft → activate → match sheet full lifecycle → close.\"\"\"\n\n        # STEP 2: Add players and activate\n        lines = self.env[\"federation.team.roster.line\"]\n        for player in self.players:\n            line = self.env[\"federation.team.roster.line\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"roster_id\": roster.id,\n                    \"player_id\": player.id,\n                    \"status\": \"active\",\n                }\n            )\n            lines |= line\n        roster.action_activate()\n        self.assertEqual(roster.status, \"active\")\n\n        # STEP 3: Create a match in 'done' state (needed to lock sheet later)\n        match = self.env[\"federation.match\"].create(\n            {\n                \"tournament_id\": self.tournament.id,\n                \"home_team_id\": self.team.id,\n                \"home_score\": 3,\n                \"away_score\": 1,\n                \"state\": \"done\",\n            }\n        )\n\n        # STEP 4: Create match sheet using side='other' to avoid team constraint\n        sheet = self.env[\"federation.match.sheet\"].create(\n            {\n                \"match_id\": match.id,\n                \"team_id\": self.team.id,\n                \"side\": \"other\",\n                \"roster_id\": roster.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"draft\")\n\n        # STEP 5: Add lines — each references a roster line for eligibility\n        for player, line in zip(self.players, lines):\n            self.env[\"federation.match.sheet.line\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"match_sheet_id\": sheet.id,\n                    \"player_id\": player.id,\n                    \"roster_line_id\": line.id,\n                    \"is_starter\": True,\n                }\n            )\n\n        # STEP 8: Lock (match is already 'done')\n        sheet.action_lock()\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"locked\")\n        self.assertTrue(sheet.locked_on)\n        self.assertTrue(sheet.locked_by_id)\n\n        # {"content": "# Schedule Approval\n\nThis addon owns independent schedule review and immutable schedule publication.\nIt does not own working assignments, calendar capacity, or match-day execution.\n\n## Operator flow\n\n1. A schedule planner submits a complete schedule from **Schedule Planner**.\n2. The addon creates immutable review evidence and opens the pending review.\n3. A different assigned schedule approver opens **Schedule Review Queue**.\n4. The approver either enters a note and selects **Request Changes**, or selects\n   **Approve Schedule**.\n5. Approved reviews appear under **Publication > Approved Schedules**.\n6. **Publish Schedule** creates any missing operational matches for the assigned\n   fixtures through the fixture materializer, creates an immutable publication,\n   links matches to their exact slots, and makes the publication current for the\n   match day.\n7. **Publication > Schedule Publications** retains live and superseded evidence.\n\nThe command service enforces edition roles, separation of duties, submitted\nrevision equality, snapshot-digest equality for schedule facts, and schedule\nrevalidation. Operational match links are derived and may be materialized at\npublication. Buttons are only orchestration entry points and never duplicate\nthe business rules.\nRole assignments remain administrator-managed; the Schedule Approver group\nexposes the workflow actions, while a per-edition `schedule_approver` assignment\nauthorizes the operation. The role check performs a read-only internal lookup,\nand approval revalidation performs controlled read-only access to the submitted\ncalendar and venue data, so approvers do not need CRUD access to those\nadministrator-managed records. Reviewers may edit the note while a review is\npending; state and audit fields remain command-service-only.\n\n## Tests and contracts\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_competition_pipeline_contract.py\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## 5.1.1 integrity rules\n\nReview evidence is immutable through the model guard. Pending reviewers may edit\nonly the note; only the approval command service can write decision fields\nthrough a narrowly scoped context. Publications are live,\nversioned and replaced per match day, not per edition. Publication confirmation\nlocks the match day and verifies the expected current publication before\nallocating the next version. Replacements require a dedicated reason that is\nseparate from the review note.\n", "content_length": 2540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_schedule_approval/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "f09718912ae4aff8fcea4b97c10df0edcbbf6111083e8a36182c70b4c5fe6053", "size_bytes": 2540}

{"content": "# Sports Federation Scheduling\n\nThe scheduling addon owns working schedules, fixture assignments, schedule\nchanges, and the weighted fairness auto-schedule preview.\n\nThe auto-schedule wizard previews deterministic assignments after applying hard\nconstraints and weighted fairness penalties. Applying a proposal records the\nautomatic assignments and schedule changes while checking the schedule revision\nfor concurrent edits.\n\nAll access-control rows, including the auto-schedule wizard permissions, are\nloaded through `security/ir.model.access.csv`.\n\n\n## Operator handoff to independent review\n\nA planner completes fixture-to-slot assignments in **Schedule Planner** and uses\n**Submit for Review**. Blocking validation errors prevent submission. When only\nwarnings remain, a confirmation dialog requires an explicit justification. The\nbutton delegates to `federation.schedule.commands`; when Schedule Approval is\ninstalled, the approval extension creates the immutable pending review in the\nsame transaction and opens it directly.\n\nSubmitted schedules are immutable. If a reviewer requests changes, the schedule\nreturns to `changes_requested`, where the planner can edit and submit a new\nrevision. Planners can use the **Reviews** smart button to inspect the current\nhandoff and retained history.\n", "content_length": 1297, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_scheduling/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "5739035035f9d4bd235fa1da1e9642c79bb0ee7d94ffcf3a5f662c6e2bc211b7", "size_bytes": 1297}

{"content": "Sports Federation Standings\n===========================\n\nComputes and stores league-style standings tables for tournament stages and\ngroups. Aggregates match results into a ranked table with points, wins,\nlosses, goal differences, and configurable tie-break ordering.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a snapshot of competition standings that can be published, audited,\nand used by downstream modules such as the public site, reporting, and\nqualification logic. Standings are linked to rule sets to ensure consistent\nscoring and tie resolution.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments, stages, groups, and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Rule sets for scoring and tie-breaks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.standing``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA standings table for a specific scope such as a tournament, stage, or group.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Standings title.\n- ``tournament_id`` (Many2one): Tournament.\n- ``stage_id`` (Many2one): Optional stage scope.\n- ``group_id`` (Many2one): Optional group scope.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Competition context.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Scoring and tie-break rules.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``computed``, or ``frozen``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Ranked team entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``computed_on`` (Datetime): When the table was last computed.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Additional notes.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> computed -> frozen``.\n\n``federation.standing.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nOne row per participant in the standings table.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Parent standings.\n- ``participant_id`` (Many2one): The team.\n- ``rank`` (Integer): Position in the standings table (1 = first).\n- ``played`` (Integer): Total matches played.\n- ``won`` / ``drawn`` / ``lost`` (Integer): Results breakdown.\n- ``score_for`` / ``score_against`` (Integer): Goals/points scored and conceded.\n- ``score_diff`` (Integer, computed): ``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the attached rule\n   set and its configured win, draw, and loss values.\n- **Tie-break resolution**: when teams have equal points, tie-break rules from\n   the rule set are applied in sequence order.\n- **Snapshot model**: each standings record is a point-in-time computation,\n   allowing historical comparison.\n- **Official-result filtering**: when ``sports_federation_result_control`` is\n   installed, only matches with ``include_in_official_standings = True`` are\n   counted.\n- **Freeze behavior**: frozen standings reject recomputation unless\n   ``force_recompute`` is provided in context.\n- **Auto-advance hook**: freezing a standing can trigger pending\n   ``federation.stage.progression`` rules with ``auto_advance = True``.\n- **Publication is separate**: public visibility is handled by\n   ``sports_federation_public_site`` through ``website_published``, not by a\n   dedicated published standings state.\n- **Optional queued recompute**: standings can be recomputed asynchronously via\n   ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` and the\n   ``action_queue_recompute`` button.\n- **Idempotent queue requests**: repeated queue requests with the same\n   ``idempotency_key`` replay the original job instead of creating duplicates.\n- **Queue visibility**: pending and failed queue counters are surfaced directly\n   on the standing form, with a dedicated queue action and menu entry.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\n- Adds ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` for asynchronous, idempotent\n   standings recompute processing.\n- Adds queue cron ``Standings: Process Recompute Queue``.\n", "content_length": 4709, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_standings/README.md", {"content": "# Sports Federation Tournament\n\nTournament lifecycle management — from creation through scheduling to completion.\nProvides the structural backbone for all competitive activity: tournaments, stages,\ngroups, participants, and matches.\n\n## Purpose\n\nModels the full **tournament hierarchy**: a tournament is divided into stages\n(e.g. group phase, quarter-finals), stages contain groups, and groups contain\nmatches between participants. This module is the central hub that most\ncompetition-related modules extend.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets, competitions |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.competition`\n\nA named competition series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\") that may span\nmultiple seasons and link to a rule set.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Competition identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Governing season |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Applicable rule set |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / active / closed |\n| `tournament_ids` | One2many | Tournaments under this competition |\n\n### `federation.season` extension\n\nThe module extends seasons with a tournament relation and a dedicated tournament\ncount stat used by the season form shortcut into related tournaments.\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\nA single tournament event within a competition or season.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Tournament identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season context |\n| `competition_id` | Many2one | Parent competition |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Rules (inherited from competition or set directly) |\n| `tournament_type` | Selection | league / cup / friendly / playoff |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / open / in_progress / closed / cancelled |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Event window |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Participant cap |\n| `stage_ids` | One2many | Tournament stages |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Enrolled participants |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | All matches across stages |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → open → in_progress → closed / cancelled.\n- **Stat buttons** for stages, participants, and matches.\n\n### `federation.tournament.stage`\n\nA phase or round within a tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Semi-finals\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Stage label |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Parent tournament |\n| `stage_type` | Selection | group / knockout / playoff / other |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Stage window |\n| `group_ids` | One2many | Groups within this stage |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Matches in this stage |\n\n### `federation.tournament.group`\n\nA subdivision within a stage (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Group label |\n| `stage_id` | Many2one | Parent stage |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Computed from stage |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Group capacity |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Teams in this group |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Group matches |\n\n### `federation.tournament.participant`\n\nLinks a team to a tournament, optionally assigned to a specific stage and group.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | Team name in tournament context |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `team_id` | Many2one | The team |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Computed from team |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Assignment |\n| `seed` | Integer | Seeding rank |\n| `registration_date` | Date | When enrolled |\n| `state` | Selection | registered / confirmed / withdrawn / eliminated |\n\n### `federation.match`\n\nAn individual game between two teams.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | \"Home vs Away\" |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Location in hierarchy |\n| `round_id` | Many2one | Single-day round assignment |\n| `home_team_id` / `away_team_id` | Many2one | Competing teams |\n| `date_scheduled` | Datetime | Stored kickoff datetime for downstream integrations |\n| `scheduled_date` | Date (computed) | Inherited from the assigned round |\n| `scheduled_time` | Float | Editable match kickoff time-of-day |\n| `home_score` / `away_score` | Integer | Final score |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / scheduled / in_progress / done / cancelled |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done / cancelled.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Hierarchical structure** — Tournament → Stage → Group → Match.\n2. **Participant tracking** — Teams enrol in a tournament and are placed into stages/groups.\n3. **Score entry** — Match results are recorded with home/away scores.\n4. **State management** — Both tournaments and matches follow state machines that\n   prevent illogical transitions.\n5. **Round-owned scheduling** — Rounds are single-day containers. A match assigned to a round inherits that round's calendar date and only stores its own kickoff time.\n6. **Stage windows** — Stages remain the broader multi-day grouping above rounds.\n7. **Tournament open/start guards** — Only active draft tournaments linked to a season can open, and only open tournaments with at least one stage can start.\n8. **Archive safety** — Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before archiving.\n9. **Venue extensions** — Venue fields are supplied by `sports_federation_venues`; this module keeps the core match lifecycle and hierarchy only.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.1.0)\n\n- Added migration scripts under `migrations/19.0.1.1.0/` to harden `federation.match` indexing for high-traffic filters.\n- Added backfill for `scheduled_date` and `round_number` on historical match rows where those persisted values were missing.\n- Added composite indexes for `(tournament_id, state)`, `(stage_id, state)`, `(group_id, state)`, `(scheduled_date, state)`, and `(date_scheduled, state)`.\n\n## Knockout result resolution (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\nKnockout matches must have an unambiguous advancing team before they can be\ncompleted. A tied numeric score requires a non-regulation resolution, such as\novertime, tiebreak, forfeit, walkover, or an administrative decision, plus an\nexplicit advancing team selected from the two match participants.\n\nWinner and loser bracket progression uses this explicit decision, preventing a\ncompleted knockout match from leaving downstream participants unresolved.\n", "content_length": 6639, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_tournament/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3bf73f9207c54b0d3b527f74a84d44b7e21e216f6a3f91489177bce88e6b76a3", "size_bytes": 6677}

{"content": "Sports Federation Venues\n========================\n\nVenue, playing-area, and round scheduling support. Tracks physical locations\nwhere matches are held, including address, capacity, facilities, individual\nplaying surfaces, and round-level venue assignment.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nCentralizes venue information so tournaments, rounds, and matches can use\nstructured location data instead of free-text fields. Playing areas let a\nsingle venue, such as a sports complex, contain multiple usable surfaces.\nRounds carry the shared schedule metadata for a block of matches: the calendar\ndate and venue live on the round, while each match keeps its own exact kickoff\ntime.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Core entities.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments and matches.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.venue``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA physical location such as a stadium, sports hall, or complex.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Venue name.\n- ``street`` through ``country_id`` (Address): Full postal address.\n- ``contact_name`` / ``contact_email`` / ``contact_phone`` (Char): On-site\n  contact details.\n- ``capacity`` (Integer): Total spectator capacity.\n- ``equipment_notes`` (Text): Available equipment.\n- ``playing_area_ids`` (One2many): Courts, pitches, and other playable areas.\n- ``blackout_window_ids`` (One2many): Venue or playing-area blackout windows.\n- ``playing_area_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``blackout_window_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``notes`` (Text): General notes.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the venue is in use.\n\n``federation.playing.area``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA single playing surface within a venue.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Area label such as ``Pitch 1``.\n- ``venue_id`` (Many2one): Parent venue.\n- ``code`` (Char): Short code.\n- ``capacity`` (Integer): Surface-specific capacity.\n- ``surface_type`` (Selection): ``grass``, ``artificial``, ``indoor``,\n  ``clay``, or ``other``.\n- ``capability_ids`` (Many2many): Capability tags such as lighting,\n  streaming, or sport-specific equipment.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the area is available.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n``federation.playing.area.capability``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA reusable tag that describes what a playing area can support.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Capability label.\n- ``code`` (Char): Stable short code.\n- ``description`` (Text): Optional operator notes.\n\n``federation.venue.blackout``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA closure or blackout window that makes a venue or one playing area unavailable.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Operator-facing label.\n- ``venue_id`` (Many2one): Affected venue.\n- ``playing_area_id`` (Many2one): Optional specific playing area.\n- ``date_start`` / ``date_end`` (Datetime): Closed interval.\n- ``reason`` (Selection): ``blackout``, ``maintenance``, or ``other``.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Optional scheduling notes.\n\nInherited Extensions\n--------------------\n\n- ``federation.tournament`` gains ``venue_id`` and ``venue_notes`` for\n  tournament-wide venue planning notes plus\n  ``required_playing_area_capability_ids`` for divisions that need specific\n  courts.\n- ``federation.tournament.stage`` surfaces linked ``round_ids`` so stage admins\n  can plan sequence, date, and venue directly on rounds.\n- ``federation.tournament.round`` gains ``venue_id`` alongside the base\n  ``round_date`` field from the tournament module.\n- ``federation.match`` gains ``venue_id`` and ``playing_area_id``. When a\n  match is linked to a round, the round becomes the authoritative shared\n  venue/date scope.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Structured addresses**: venues store full addresses with country\n  references.\n- **Multi-area venues**: a sports complex can have several pitches or courts.\n- **Constraint windows**: venues can declare blackout or maintenance windows at\n  venue or playing-area level.\n- **Capability tags**: playing areas can advertise the operational capabilities\n  they support, and divisions can require matching capabilities.\n- **Round-owned schedule planning**: administrators can create stage rounds up\n  front and assign a date and venue to each one without duplicating scheduling\n  concepts.\n- **Match to round consistency**: assigning a round to a match propagates the\n  tournament and stage scope, applies the round venue, and rejects conflicting\n  venue or date combinations.\n- **Duplicate-pairing guardrails**: teams in the same category cannot play the\n  same opponent more than once inside the same round.\n- **Scheduling integration**: blackout windows, maintenance closures, and\n  capability mismatches are validated by the scheduling workflow before a\n  schedule can be approved.\n- **Finance bridge integration**: when ``sports_federation_finance_bridge`` is\n  installed, scheduling a match with a venue automatically creates or reuses a\n  draft venue-booking charge for passthrough settlement.\n", "content_length": 4924, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_venues/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "b38573da273084eef42de4ea8ae7e354571452133d458891a505ba27574d36fd", "size_bytes": 4924}
